items.title: Pastor sues OpenAI over ChatGPT medical advice; $1B in Medicaid payments frozen; CMS says surprise billing law is being 'gamed' — Morning Medical Update Weekly Recap - Medical Economics
items.reason: The item explicitly mentions CMS stating that the surprise billing law (No Surprises Act) is being 'gamed,' which directly addresses enforcement and implementation challenges relevant to litigation and rule interpretation.
items.summary: According to a Medical Economics weekly recap, CMS has stated that the surprise billing law is being 'gamed,' indicating enforcement concerns with the No Surprises Act implementation. While the excerpt itself is limited and lacks specific details about which CMS official made the statement, the rule or regulation being referenced, or concrete examples of the alleged gaming, this development signals potential regulatory action or interpretation adjustments by CMS regarding surprise billing protections. This matters for revenue-cycle teams as it suggests CMS may be tightening enforcement or clarifying rules around how the No Surprises Act is being applied, which could affect balance-billing practices and Independent Dispute Resolution processes.
